newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak rates ease but further falls seen unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Slovak rates ease but further falls seen unlikely.

text.p: Slovak interbank money rates dipped below 20 percent on Wednesday, but traders said a further fall was unlikely as some local banks remained short of crowns.
"Rates have eased but the fall occured only because a few local banks, which are still short of crowns, are not willing to accept high prices," said one Bratislava-based trader.

"We cannot talk about a regular market as the banks still do not have to quote offers on crowns so some banks will lend you money at over 30 percent but they would only borrow it for 12 (percent)," the dealer said.

Martin Hrozany of Credit Lyonnais said a further decline in rates was not probable since the central bank (NBS) would drain five billion crowns from the market when one of its repo tenders mature on Thursday.

"We have to wait to see if the NBS adds some crowns tomorrow...if it does not complement the market, rates can rise, but even if the bank adds some liquidity, they (rates) should not go down much below 17-18 percent," Hrozany said.
Interbank rates rose to above 35 percent three weeks ago after the NBS squeezed market liquidity to battle speculative pressure on the crown.
Crown rates have hovered between mark/dollar basket parity and -1.0 percent on the band's weak side over the past two weeks, but the interbank market remains illiquid.
The NBS gradually adds crowns through short-term repo tenders, keeping the banking sector short of funds required for minimum reserves requirements.
